Tier Projects Characteristics
Tier 1 — Industrial Scale OpenClaw 500+ items/24h; LTS track; governance in releases; but P0 debt unpaid
Tier 2 — Rapid Iteration Hermes, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw 35–50 items/24h; 1–16 closures; 0–1 releases; growing or clearing backlogs
Tier 3 — Dormant IronClaw No activity

Momentum Assessment

  • Rapidly iterating: Hermes (unification PRs stacked, Webapp post-merge churn) and QwenPaw (healthy 20:15 close ratio, active first-time contributors, vendor participation from Firecrawl).
  • Stabilizing / hardening: ZeroClaw (v0.8.7 security follow-up, coordinated OIDC review) and OpenClaw (release notes read as bug-fix-oriented — "hardening after rapid growth").
  • At risk of bit-rot: ZeroClaw's merge ratio (1 closed / 39 open), QwenPaw's XXXL PRs (#7874 SDK redesign open 5.5 weeks, #7785 voice chat open 6 weeks), and Hermes' stale-but-valid PRs (#71743 open 3 months, #70493 open 3 months).

Maturity Signals

  • Highest maturity: OpenClaw (LTS, ACL, authority boundaries) and QwenPaw (audit DB, governance layer).
  • Emerging maturity: ZeroClaw (OIDC dashboard tagged for v0.9.0, per-agent knowledge-graph scoping #9745).
  • Maturity gap: Hermes lacks a release in 24h despite 16 merged PRs and a P2 session regression (#143831 on v0.22.4) — a patch release is overdue.

7. Trend Signals

For AI agent developers, the following industry trends are extractable from this 24-hour snapshot:

1. Single-threaded gateways are the ecosystem's hard ceiling.

Every active project has a P0/P1 issue rooted in synchronous persistence, plugin capture, or SQLite contention blocking the event loop (OpenClaw #160959/#119720/#117262, Hermes #143256/#144883). Actionable: Design agents with async-safe state layers from day one — retrofitting is the dominant cost in mature projects.

2. Context compaction is the new reliability frontier.

QwenPaw treats it as its #1 cliff; OpenClaw measures cache-token waste (21.3M) and dropped terminal facts; Hermes has a community RFC on a "doc-chain substrate." Actionable: Treat compaction as a first-class, structured-data-preserving, provenance-aware subsystem — not a text summarizer.

3. Multi-surface = multi-identity, and identity is unsolved.

Hermes' six not_found bugs across five surfaces, OpenClaw's multi-agent binding conflicts (#115354), and ZeroClaw's principal-scoping cluster all point to the same gap. Actionable: Define an explicit session/principal ownership model before shipping a second surface.

4. Security is shifting from perimeter to principal.

ZeroClaw's coordinated #12046–#12052 review (wildcard tool selectors, OIDC limiters, XFF spoofing), OpenClaw's authority-preservation release notes, and the long-pending filesystem sandboxing request (#7722) all signal the same shift. Actionable: Per-principal capability grants (not per-channel or per-role) are becoming table stakes.

5. OAuth/entitlement reuse is a top recurring user request.

Two separate closed threads on QwenPaw (#1536, #4124) requesting OAuth for Codex/OpenAI, plus ZeroClaw's OIDC dashboard push, indicate users want to reuse existing subscriptions rather than manage API keys. Actionable: Provider OAuth is a differentiator — and a compliance requirement in enterprise deployments.

6. Windows and mobile remain second-class platforms.

OpenClaw (schtasks, ACL, npm cleanup — release blocker #170956), Hermes (Windows ARM64 build #145723, SSH-to-Windows #136574, iOS/Android session adoption), QwenPaw (log rotation, UI blanking, Creator deletion), ZeroClaw (Android shell always fails #12075) — every project has Windows or mobile gaps. Actionable: Cross-platform correctness is an under-served moat; it is also where the loudest users are.

7. Silent failure is the sharpest trust destroyer.

Hermes' 110-message silent loss (#145556), QwenPaw's silent audit-DB stop (#8412) and silent channel disable (#8406), ZeroClaw's silent prompt drop on reload (#11517), OpenClaw's masked-password 4-hour misdiagnosis (#173313) — users consistently rate silent failure worse than loud failure. Actionable: Every degradation path needs a visible signal; masked values must announce they are masked.

8. Large-PR risk is systemic.

XXXL/XL PRs stall across all projects (QwenPaw #7874/#7785, ZeroClaw #11414/#11596 relay, Hermes #122509, OpenClaw's GitLab #185928). Actionable for contributors: Decompose. For maintainers: Anti-bit-rot rotation is needed — ZeroClaw's #9745 (release-gate, 12 weeks open, needs-author-action) is the cautionary example.

Ecosystem-level recommendation: The next 30 days should be watched for (a) whether OpenClaw ships a dedicated "Gateway contention + Windows" reliability release, (b) whether Hermes cuts a patch release with the session-unification stack, and (c) whether ZeroClaw closes the security cluster #12046–#12052. S2 — Degraded behavior

  • #11517 — Web chat reload mid-turn drops prompt from screen and localStorage (hydration overwrites local state with a pre-turn snapshot). No fix PR.
  • #12055 — MCP HTTP client has no pool/keep-alive control; stale pooled socket loses tool call as outcome-unknown. No fix PR. (Related to #10807 transport family.)
  • #12072 — Codex stream-decode fallback retries with stream:false, which the default ChatGPT endpoint always rejects (400). Fix PR: #12073 (open).
  • #12064 — Discord plaintext approvals answerable by an allowlisted peer bot. Fix PR: #12065 (open).
  • #12047 — OIDC bearer verification on gateway routes lacks attempt limiter/outbound cap → resource exhaustion. No fix PR.
  • #12049 — Sign-in flow store (32 slots, 8/address, 10 min) can be filled by 4 addresses, locking out everyone incl. loopback. No fix PR.
  • #12052 — Limiters key on first X-Forwarded-For entry → client behind appending proxy can spoof loopback exemption. No fix PR.
  • #12051 — sop_workshop apply lets a scoped principal author shared SOPs that later run with operator authority (privilege escalation). No fix PR.
  • #12046 — Non-admin principals with wildcard tool selector retain principal-unaware tools (cron, schedule, peer messaging, SOP execution). No fix PR.

S3 — Minor

  • #12067 — untrusted_guard_sensitivity moves prompt guard and leak detector in opposite directions (doc says higher = stricter; code disagrees). No fix PR.
  • #12066 — Prompt guard flags any bare ; or | as command injection → most clean SOP payloads return Suspicious. Fix PR: #12068 (open).

Stability read: The identity/access cluster (#12046–#12052, authored largely by the same reporter) reads like a coordinated security review and is the most important stability signal in this digest. None of those have fix PRs yet.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Request Issue Signal strength Likely timing
Dashboard sign-in with OIDC #11961 Tagged release:v0.9.0 v0.9.0 — explicit milestone.
/load-session in ZeroCode Code pane #12069 PR #12071 already open Near-term (next minor).
max reasoning effort for compatible OpenAI models #10705 Long-running (priority:p2); PR #12059 touches thinking profiles Likely v0.9.x.
Focused workspaces (web) PR #11414 risk:high, size:XL, topic:operator-ux Operator UX track, v0.9.x.
Append-only session event history PR #11921 size:XL, cross-cutting Foundational; may gate other session work.

Prediction: v0.9.0 looks positioned as the identity + session-integrity release — OIDC dashboard sign-in (#11961) plus the gateway hardening bugs (#12046–#12052) plus append-only session history (#11921). /load-session is small and PR-backed, so it may land earlier as a point release.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (verbatim themes):

  • "Reloading mid-turn drops the user's prompt" — users lose work on the default session_persistence = true path (#11517).
  • "One failed recovery attempt" permanently poisons MCP sessions — transient infra blips become hard failures (#10807, #12055).
  • "Every shell tool call fails" on Android/Termux native aarch64 — a platform regression that fully blocks the shell tool (#12075).
  • "Most clean SOP payloads come back Suspicious" — false-positive fatigue from an over-broad prompt guard (#12066, #12067).
  • Security-conscious reporters flag privilege escalation via SOP workshop (#12051) and wildcard tool selectors (#12046).

Satisfaction signals: Low comment counts on many items but high reporter precision — issues include file paths, line numbers, and severity ratings (S1–S3), suggesting a technically engaged, security-aware user base rather than casual users.

Dissatisfaction signals: Recurring frustration with state fragility (lost prompts, poisoned sessions) and overly aggressive security defaults that break legitimate workflows — a classic tension the maintainers will need to balance in v0.9.0.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention — high impact, low recent movement, or aging:

  • #10705 — Max reasoning effort for compatible OpenAI models. Open since 2026-09-07 (7+ weeks), only 1 comment. Directly affects GPT-6 Astra users. PR #12059 touches adjacent thinking-profile logic — maintainers should link these.
  • #9745 — Per-agent attribution and scoping for the knowledge graph. Open since 2026-08-04 (~12 weeks), tagged priority:p1, needs-author-action, release-gate, release:v0.9.0. This is the single oldest high-priority PR in the set and is flagged needs-author-action — it risks missing the v0.9.0 gate if it stalls further.
  • #11414 — Opt-in focused workspaces. risk:high, size:XL, open since 2026-10-01. Large operator-UX change awaiting review bandwidth.
  • #11680 — Firecrawl web search provider. needs-maintainer-review, open since 2026-10-12. External contributor (Firecrawl team) — timely review supports community goodwill.
  • #11596 — Native Claude Code accounts with supervised plugin apply. risk:high, size:XL, stacked on parent #11602 — stacked PRs risk bit-rot if the parent moves.

Maintainer recommendation: Prioritize (a) the security cluster #12046–#12052, (b) unblocking #9745 before the v0.9.0 gate, and (c) triaging the Android regression #12075 which currently has no owner or fix PR.

item.content:encoded:
AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-10-28

Generated: 2026-10-28 00:25 UTC | Projects covered: 6

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

Cross-Project Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — AI Infrastructure Ecosystem

Date: 2026-10-28 | Projects: vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, LiteLLM, Unsloth

1. Ecosystem Overview

The ecosystem is in a frontier-model enablement race rather than a serving-logic race: every engine's backlog is dominated by hardware-specific gaps (Ampere for DeepSeek-V4-Flash, SM120 graph capture, gfx950 for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash) rather than by new abstractions. A clear AMD/ROCm convergence is underway — vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, and Unsloth all landed AMD/AITER/XPU work today, but each is exposing accuracy regressions that only appear at high concurrency. Simultaneously, agent correctness is emerging as a distinct failure class: tool-call parsing, streaming semantics, and silent schema drops now occupy the highest-severity slots across llama.cpp, Ollama, SGLang, and LiteLLM. Non-engine layers (LiteLLM, Unsloth) are shipping breaking-but-security-adjacent changes today (MCP hidden-tool bypass, user-directory scoping, key expiration semantics) that shape the trust boundary more than any kernel PR.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Layer Active Issues (today) Active PRs (today) Release status (last 24h)
vLLM Server engine ~13 ranked (2 closed RFCs incl. accuracy collapse) ~8 perf PRs + model enablements No release; Q4 roadmap is canonical artifact
SGLang Server engine ~10 ranked (1 P0 spec-decode crash) ~10 (5-PR AMD gfx950 series) No release; baseline v0.5.22 referenced
llama.cpp Local runtime ~9 ranked (#25618 quant spec-decode divergence) ~5 perf + new-op PRs 4 releases (b11927 → b11938)
Ollama Local runtime ~10 ranked (#17778 tool-loop 500s, 32 👍) ~7 (2 major MLX PRs) No release; 0.40.4 as affected base
LiteLLM Gateway ~12 ranked (2 HIGH security) ~10 (guardrail cluster + backports) 4 releases (v1.106.5 / 1.105.6 / 1.104.8 / 1.103.10)
Unsloth Training/fine-tune ~10 ranked (CI breakage, Anthropic passthrough) ~10 (Studio + Benchmarks + perf) No release; stabilization push

Reading: Server engines (vLLM, SGLang) traded release cadence for kernel breadth. Local runtimes diverged — llama.cpp ships fast, Ollama stabilizes. The gateway (LiteLLM) and training layer (Unsloth) are absorbing correctness/compatibility debt into their own CI.

3. Model Support Race

Leaders by footprint today:

  • llama.cpp — broadest surface, fastest shipping. LFM3 family fully landed (base, VL, video, /v1/realtime voice, d1 decision heads), plus MiniCPM-OCR-Jev, GigaChat 3.5 432B-A28B (in review), d2t draft vocab for Qwen3.5-MoE MTP. Ships as 12 tagged builds in 24h.
  • SGLang — deepest single-model investment. Five coordinated PRs on MiniMax-M3.1-Flash for MI350X/MI355X (sparse attention, NVFP4 KV, DSpark verify, MoE/router GEMV, block-FP8 GEMM, decode indexer CP). Follows the same playbook it used for DeepSeek-V4.1.
  • vLLM — frontier enablement via long-tail trackers. DeepSeek-V4-Flash on Ampere (#50576, 121 comments), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash MXFP8/SM120, GLM-5.3, Qwen3.8, Nemotron-H MoE block configs, Gemma 4 on RDNA. Coverage is planned across many models; landing is per-body-of-work.
  • Ollama — narrow, MLX-weighted. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B with LiLiCorr spec decode (#19229) and Kolibri 1 (#18780) both open; LFM3 GGUF loading just fixed (#19344) after the "unknown architecture 'lfm3'" break.
  • LiteLLM — API-surface expansion, not kernels. xAI X Search (native with citations + billing), Morph open models, Bedrock Mantle-native Claude token counting. Cloudflare Workers AI proposals are ~10 months stale.
  • Unsloth — demand-driven backlog. LFM3-1.7B, Intel Arc B580 XPU, exllamav3, AMD iGPU VRAM fix (#14039) — all in request/queue stage, none shipped.

Winner: llama.cpp on breadth-per-hour; SGLang on depth for a single frontier model on AMD.

4. Performance Frontier

Vector Current hot spots
KV cache & offloading vLLM dominates: P2P fault semantics (#63602), GDS filesystem offload (#48504), Mooncake descriptor overhead (#63006), reusable compression RFC (#59538). SGLang: HiCache prefill fastpath re-enabled (#46884), PD+HiCache stale-KV fix (#44070).
MoE routing / EP vLLM MoETPCollectiveOptimizationPass (#63479), Triton naive-block-assignment regression (#63943); SGLang --max-payload + LoRA-PP csgmv grid bounding (#46743); llama.cpp --moe-cache-cpu-share CPU spill (#30966).
Speculative decoding vLLM structured-output distribution preservation (#62818, closed); llama.cpp quant-target divergence (#25618, open, correctness); SGLang FlashInfer verify-sampling JIT crash (#43412, open); Ollama LiLiCorr in Nemotron PR (#19229).
Kernels / fused ops SGLang DeepSeek-V4.1 mHC+combine+RMSNorm fusion (#46088), AITER GDN prefill (#39873); llama.cpp Metal fused TOP_K_MASK (b11927), Hexagon TOP_K (~42% of DFlash draft time); vLLM AITER fused AR+RMSNorm+quant (#56326).
Quantization llama.cpp OCP FP8 E4M3 saturating in ggml (#27512); vLLM FlashInfer FP8 block-scale GEMM fix (#64040); SGLang NVFP4 KV + block-FP8 GEMM for MiniMax-M3.1.
Distributed serving vLLM TP MoE collective optimization; SGLang LoRA under PP (memory + throughput); llama.cpp --models-memory-max router eviction (b11930); Ollama concurrent MLX generation (#19197).
Sampling & determinism vLLM --routing zipf for MoE bench (#64167), nondeterministic greedy (#58899); llama.cpp fused TOP_K for spec-decode draft batches; SGLang top-k/top-p consistency fix (#41916).

The unsatisfiable tension today: every engine is fusing more kernels for throughput, but at least three projects (vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp) have open correctness bugs on fused/reordered paths — determinism, distribution drift, silent divergence. Speed is no longer the only axis.

5. Layer Positioning

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ APPLICATION / AGENT LAYER                                        │
│   tool-calling loops · MCP · streaming parsers · spec decode     │
└────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
             │
┌────────────▼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ GATEWAY — LiteLLM                                                │
│   multi-provider routing · guardrails · budgets · key mgmt       │
│   exposing MCP hidden-tool bypass + secret-redaction surface     │
└────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
             │
┌────────────▼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ SERVER ENGINES — vLLM  |  SGLang                                 │
│   PD disaggregation · KV offload tiers · distributed serving     │
│   frontier-model enablement on A100/H100/H200/MI355X/SM120       │
└────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
             │
┌────────────▼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ LOCAL RUNTIMES — llama.cpp  |  Ollama                            │
│   GGUF/MLX quant · CPU/GPU/Metal/Vulkan/SYCL · on-device agents  │
│   router-mode multi-model · /v1/realtime voice · LFM3 stack      │
└────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
             │
┌────────────▼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ TRAINING / FINE-TUNING — Unsloth                                 │
│   LoRA SFT · DPO (online) · Studio UI · MLX/GGUF export          │
│   bridged to serving via llama.cpp/vLLM backends                 │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Layer differentiation is sharpening: vLLM and SGLang are converging on the same set of primitives (PD disaggregation, KV tiering, EP/TP MoE collective optimization), while llama.cpp and Ollama are converging on on-device multimodal agents (LFM3 VL/Audio/Omni, /v1/realtime voice, mini decision heads). LiteLLM and Unsloth are sandwiching the engines: one owning policy, one owning production of weights.

6. Trend Signals

1. Agent correctness is the new P0. Highest-severity items in llama.cpp (#25618 quant spec-decode divergence), Ollama (#17778 tool loop 500s, #17892 thinking loop, #19187 silent schema drop), SGLang (#35564 streaming tool-call parsers, closed as inactive), and LiteLLM (#48171 MCP hidden-tool bypass) are all agent loop failures, not throughput failures. Watch: your eval suite must exercise streaming, multi-turn, and spec-decode paths end-to-end — buffered smoke tests pass through every one of these bugs.

2. AMD is production-viable but env-var-fragile. vLLM #60160 (AITER accuracy collapse, concurrency-dependent), SGLang gfx950 illegal memory access (#48043) and SM121 QSA gap (#36558), llama.cpp ROCm split-mode garbage (#16424). Watch: pin VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER, add concurrency-swept accuracy sweeps, and gate upgrades behind gfx-target-specific tests.

3. Quantization × architecture interactions are silent killers. llama.cpp IQ3_S on RTX 5060 Ti (#28581), Ollama q2_K/q3_K of qwen2.5-coder:3b (#18252, 0/15 on functional suite), SGLang Kimi-K3 SM90 silently computes SwiGLU instead of SiTU (#45755). Watch: pin quants by hash and run a small functional eval on every quant level, not perplexity alone.

4. Gateway security boundary is being redrawn. LiteLLM's MCP hidden-tool bypass (#48171, now fixed on tools/call and pre-upstream), and the in-flight secret-redaction expansion to tool inputs, outputs, args, and system prompts (#47122) mean the same agents that were safe yesterday can leak or invoke unexpectedly today. Watch: diff guardrail coverage when you upgrade LiteLLM; verify x-litellm-applied-guardrails isn't over-reporting (#48472).

5. KV offloading is becoming a multi-tier connector, not a feature. vLLM's P2P + GDS + Mooncake + compression RFC stack is the blueprint: heterogeneous KV backends behind one abstraction. SGLang's HiCache is on the same trajectory (read-done fastpath, stale-KV fix). Watch: plan for a connector interface now; single-backend designs will be re-written next quarter.

6. Determinism is not a product guarantee — yet. vLLM #58899 (greedy nondeterminism between restarts), llama.cpp #25618 (spec-decode output differs from non-spec), SGLang top-k/top-p cross-path inconsistency (#41916). Watch: for audit-grade or regulated agent flows, disable timing-tuned reduction kernels and spec decode, or add a hash-based drift check to CI.

7. Release hygiene is bifurcating:

  • Hot release lines (llama.cpp: b11927 → b11938 in 24h; LiteLLM: four stable-lines-today) demand rolling pins and fast rollback.
  • Frozen release lines (vLLM, SGLang Q4 roadmaps; Ollama's 0.40.4 known-broken on /v1/systemone; Windows CUDA prebuilt stuck at b11828) mean "latest tag" ≠ "latest fix." Ask for the PR, not the version.
  • CI itself is a risk surface: Unsloth torch-config drift breaks 55–70 errors per PR; llama.cpp BYOG evals RFC (#61698) and vLLM's Zipf MoE bench (#64167) are attempts to make perf claims reproducible — but coverage is uneven across projects.

What to do next quarter:

  1. Add streaming + spec-decode + multi-turn cases to your eval gate — they're where the current silent faults live.
  2. Pin every quant, ROCm AITER env var, and guardrail config by artifact hash, not by version string.
  3. Assume one KV backend won't be enough: design an offloading connector.
  4. Treat LiteLLM guardrail updates as security upgrades — read the PR diff before deploying.
  5. If you're integrating agents through MCP or browser tools, Unsloth #14348 (per-tool switches) and current SGLang/Ollama tool-parser bugs are the config surface you'll need to test against.

Per-Project Reports

vLLM — vllm-project/vllm

vLLM Digest — 2026-10-28

1. Today's Highlights

No releases landed in the last 24h, but the queue is dominated by frontier-model enablement: DeepSeek-V4-Flash on Ampere (SM8x), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash CUDA-graph capture on SM120 Blackwell, and GLM-5.3 / Qwen3.8 optimization trackers. On the infra side, the Q4 2026 roadmap (#61024) is now the canonical planning artifact, and KV offloading/compression continues to attract the most design debate. Notably, two accuracy-sensitive RFCs closed today: structured-output + speculative decoding distribution preservation (#62818) and the ROCm AITER accuracy regression (#60160).

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

None in the last 24h. No API or config changes were announced. The Q4 2026 roadmap (#61024) is worth tracking as the source of upcoming compatibility work across SIGs.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • DeepSeek-V4-Flash on SM8x (Ampere A100/A800, RTX 30xx) — feature request with heavy community traction (121 comments, 16 👍). Neither the original nor the 0731 checkpoint runs on Ampere today; tracked at #50576.
  • Qwen3-ASR checkpoints on the Rust frontend — startup failure due to missing tokenizer.json and nested vocab_size; blocks serving the official ASR checkpoints via VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 (#61057).
  • Muse Spark AMD MonoKernel on MI350P — decode path is hard-wired to MI355X's 256 CUs and refuses to run on the 128-CU MI350P despite the same gfx950 ISA (#63712).
  • Nemotron-H heterogeneous MoE — PR adds per-layer block_configs fallback so "puzzle" variants (e.g. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B, 12 distinct MoE configs) load correctly (#62362).
  • FlashInfer attention sinks with fp8/NVFP4 KV cache — prefill path unblocked; NVFP4 served via fa2 paged prefill with epilogue sink rescale (SM12x-only for the NVFP4 case) (#63826).
  • Gemma 4 on RDNA — ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN extended to D=512 for Gemma 4's mixed D=256/D=512 attention on Radeon AI PRO R9700 (#62666).

4. Performance & Optimization

  • DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash MXFP8 decode — pinning low-latency GEMM tactics for TP8 without autotuning, stacked on #64146/#64144 (#64147).
  • TP MoE collective optimization — new torch.compile pass (MoETPCollectiveOptimizationPass) sharding output projections to reduce all-reduce/all-gather traffic; also modifies a Triton TP-sharding kernel (#63479).
  • Triton MoE naive block assignment regression — on GB10, _prepare_expert_assignment re-reads shared experts for device-resident weights, costing 8% to 2× decode slowdown when num_tokens * top_k * 4 <= num_experts (#63943).
  • ROCm MI355X trackers — Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B (#57149, 26 comments) and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (#59575) remain the largest active perf plans; both land as stacked PRs on main.
  • ROCm DSA indexer — PR allows native decode above next_n=2 via VLLM_ROCM_INDEXER_NATIVE_DECODE_MAX_NEXT_N, avoiding row-flattening re-reads for MTP with 2+ draft tokens (#59421); a separate PR routes paged MQA logits through AITER's paged_mqa_logits so kernel selection lives in AITER (#60042).
  • DeepSeek R1 on AMD — fused AR + RMSNorm + per-token quant (all KLL-bound), mirroring ATOM (#56326).
  • GLM-5.3 — optimization follow-up on the shared glm_moe_dsa architecture; CUDA work planned (#57406).
  • Dynamic PDL enablement — feature request to auto-enable TRTLLM_ENABLE_PDL / TORCHINDUCTOR_ENABLE_PDL rather than requiring undocumented flags (#40543).
  • Benchmarking — vllm bench forward gains --routing zipf (α=1.25) for skewed synthetic MoE routing with dummy weights; auto picks Zipf for dummy weights and real routing otherwise (#64167).

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. ROCm AITER accuracy collapse — Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (TP4, MI355X) at high concurrency with VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1; fine with AITER off. Closed (#60160).
  2. Structured-output + spec-decode distribution drift — StructuredOutputManager trimming draft tokens without committing grammar state can skew output distribution; RFC closed (#62818).
  3. SM120 CUDA graph capture unusable for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash — 8×TP on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell gives extremely low decode throughput with --enforce-eager; graphs unusable. Requesting priority on SM120 graph capture (#56892).
  4. P2P KV offload tier doesn't fail fast on peer faults — H200 + NIXL 1.5.0 + OffloadingConnector reproducer; missing fast-fail semantics on peer failure (#63602).
  5. Greedy output nondeterminism — q/k-norm + RoPE combo kernel picks reduction config by timing, so greedy output changes between restarts even with VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 (#58899).
  6. Rust frontend 500s on auto tool parser resolution failure — every request returns 500 when auto can't resolve a parser for the model (#63584); a separate Rust completions echo + return_token_ids fix is open (#62684).
  7. Gemma Qwen4Exp PLE n-gram padding under piecewise CUDA graphs — ROCm replays read stale query_start_loc/ngram_context rows; fix PR open (#62675).
  8. SM90 FlashInfer FP8 block-scale GEMM wrong results — kernel binding assumes row-contiguous activations; fix passes packed rows (#64040).
  9. FlashInfer one-sided workspace leak — EPLB communicator teardown didn't release all-to-all resources; fix PR open (#63874).
  10. CPU offload num_cpu_blocks inconsistency across PP ranks — 4×B300, PP4 reproducer; upstream fix proposed (#50821).
  11. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash tool calls strip Persian half-spaces (U+200C) — tokenizer/tool-parser interaction, breaking Persian output (#63794).
  12. ROCm Triton paged attention illegal memory access on gfx950 — hipErrorLaunchFailure under long-context decode on MI350X (#48043).
  13. Qwen3.6-27B spurious "System message must be at the beginning" (#41114).

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Frontier-model coverage is the bottleneck, not serving logic. DeepSeek-V4-Flash on Ampere and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on SM120 are both blocked by hardware-specific gaps. If you're choosing accelerators today, verify graph-capture support for your target model/GPU pair before committing.
  • ROCm is production-viable but kernel-version-sensitive. The AITER accuracy collapse (#60160) shows that a single env var can flip accuracy at high concurrency. Pin your VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER setting and add a concurrency-swept accuracy check to CI.
  • Determinism is not yet a guarantee. Greedy decoding can vary across restarts (#58899). If your agent depends on reproducible outputs, avoid torch.compile-tuned reduction kernels or pin the reduction config.
  • The Rust frontend is close but not drop-in. Auto tool-parser resolution and tokenizer edge cases (#63584, #61057) mean Python remains the safer default for tool-calling workloads.
  • KV offloading is becoming a multi-tier design surface. P2P tier fault semantics (#63602), GDS for filesystem offload (#48504), Mooncake descriptor overhead (#63006), and a reusable KV compression layer RFC (#59538) all landed in the last weeks. Plan for a connector abstraction rather than a single offload backend.
  • Benchmarking for MoE routing is improving. Zipf routing in vllm bench forward (#64167) plus the BYOG evals RFC (#61698) should make PR-level perf claims easier to reproduce on your own hardware.
SGLang — sgl-project/sglang

SGLang Digest — 2026-10-28

1. Today's Highlights

No releases shipped in the last 24h, but activity is dominated by two themes: an aggressive AMD/gfx950 enablement push for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (PRs #46690, #46691, #46692, #46693, #46694) and continued DeepSeek-V4.1 decode kernel fusion work (#46088). The Q4 roadmaps for PD Disaggregation (#43699) and SGLang-Diffusion (#43313) are actively being refined, signaling the strategic priorities for the next quarter. Meanwhile, the flaky-CI tracker (#42752) continues to accumulate 134+ comments, indicating ongoing friction in PR velocity.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

None in the last 24h. Note however that several closed bugs reference version v0.5.22 and main at ce66b3ab as affected baselines (e.g., #45755), so if you're tracking a specific bug fix, confirm the commit is in your pin.

Two minor API additions are in-flight:

  • --max-payload-size server flag for HTTP bodies (fixes Uvicorn/Granian default limits for base64 multimodal payloads) — PR #46482
  • Consistency fix for top-k/top-p sampling across sampling paths (supersedes earlier attempt) — PR #41916

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • MiniMax-M3.1-Flash on AMD MI350X/MI355X (gfx950): Full bring-up of sparse attention, NVFP4 KV cache, DSpark verify kernels, MoE/router GEMV, block-FP8 GEMM, and decode indexer CP. This is a multi-PR series on main with callers landing in #46693. (#46690, #46691, #46692, #46693, #46694)
  • Muse Spark Open on MI35x: New nightly accuracy gate (GSM8K + MMMU) covering both FP4 cookbook cells. (#44586)
  • XPU simple enablements consolidated into a single reviewable PR as part of the weekly XPU model-enablement lifecycle. (#46623)
  • AMD monokernels: New daily pin-bump automation for sgl-amd-mono, needed for GLM-5.3 FP8 E4M3 KV cache monokernel. (#46685)

Closed/inactive hardware gaps worth noting (no active fix landed):

  • QSA decode has no working kernel on SM121 (GB10 / DGX Spark) — Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is unservable on that arch. (#36558)
  • Apple Silicon serving redesign still in RFC: Torch-owned SRT path with whole-model MLX region export. (#32321)

4. Performance & Optimization

  • DeepSeek-V4.1 decode: fuse mHC post + four-stream combine + RMSNorm into a single kernel, removing back-to-back small kernel launches at every layer boundary in decode and target-verify. (#46088)
  • LoRA under pipeline parallelism: throughput and GPU memory improvements for multi-LoRA serving with PP; also bound csgmv CUDA-graph segment grids by token count (was sized to the max captured batch, wasting launch slots). (#45951, #46743)
  • HiCache prefill read-done fastpath re-enabled when offload copies are fenced on the forward stream — avoids falling back to wait_stream(forward_stream) and lets the schedule stream run ahead. (#46884)
  • Decode transfer queue: stop device admission at the first refusal rather than probing every later host-staged request near a full KV pool. (#46898)
  • Qwen3-Next GDN prefill: consume the AITER fused kernel to eliminate a 4-kernel chain and intermediate tensor round-trips. (#39873)
  • GLM-5.3-Flash on Hopper (SM90) optimization tracking issue opened. (#45373)

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. Speculative decoding crashes server on first non-greedy request — FlashInfer verify-sampling JIT fails on pip-installed bundles without system CUDA toolkit (bundled cccl vs pip cu13 mismatch), and the process tree is SIGKILLed. Greedy traffic is unaffected, so this can hide in staging. Open, no fix PR yet. (#43412)
  2. EP2 (tp=2 + ep=2) illegal memory access on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 (RTX PRO 6000, sm_120) — reproduced on two builds. Open. (#44291)
  3. Kimi-K3 on SM90: flashinfer_mxfp4 silently computes GPT-OSS SwiGLU instead of SiTU — silent numerical divergence in the MoE activation; the referenced upstream fix (flashinfer#4209) is still open. Open. (#45755)
  4. PD prefill + HiCache: stale KV on decode — early cached-prefix send can transfer KV before the HiCache load-back finishes when a prefix lives only in host memory. Now closed, check the fix is in your pin. (#44070)
  5. FlashInfer autotune cache discarded every boot under MoE EP>1 — per-rank shapes never agree, so the fused-MoE tactic is re-drawn each start (adds startup latency). Open. (#40320)
  6. Non-causal sliding-window attention ignored in TorchNativeAttnBackend — correctness bug on a fallback path. Open. (#39300)
  7. 8 tool-call parsers emit wrong/missing calls under token-by-token streaming — directly hits agent reliability; closed as inactive without an obvious fix reference. (#35564)
  8. Dynamic LoRA loading unsupported with --tokenizer-worker-num > 1 — per-worker registry, no cross-worker sync. Closed/inactive. (#31084)
  9. BF16 RL weight update with moe_runner_backend=flashinfer_trtllm crashes — blocked/padded w13 layout not restored on update_weights_from_tensor. Closed/inactive. (#27787)
  10. FP8 DeepSeek-V4-Flash on MI300X (gfx942) degrades with context — coherent <100 tokens, garbage by ~300, NIAH 0/3. Closed/inactive. (#36390)

Also notable: deepseek_nextn hardcodes quant_config=None for modelopt_fp4, breaking quantized NextN drafts (GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 spec decoding) — closed, #36599; and ModelOptFp4Config.is_layer_excluded misses fused and model.-prefixed names, crashing mixed-precision NVFP4 loads — closed, #36596.

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • If you're on AMD MI35x and running MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, the gfx950 kernel series is converging on main in review order; pin to main only after #46693 (the callers PR) — the earlier kernel PRs are inert alone.
  • If you enable speculative decoding on a pip-installed environment without a system CUDA toolkit, you're exposed to #43412. Greedy-only smoke tests will not catch it. Validate with at least one sampled request in your deploy gate.
  • Multimodal or agent apps sending large JSON bodies should watch #46482 for the --max-payload-size flag; until then, put a reverse proxy in front or chunk base64 payloads.
  • Agent builders relying on streaming tool calls: #35564 documents multiple parsers producing wrong token-by-token output. If you're on an affected parser, test with stream=True end-to-end, not just buffered mode.
  • LoRA-heavy multi-tenant serving with PP gets meaningful memory and throughput wins from #45951 once merged.
  • HiCache + PD disaggregation operators: the stale-KV fix in #44070 is closed, but verify your pin — the bug is silent (correct-looking output with wrong KV), which is the worst class for production debugging.

llama.cpp Digest — 2026-10-28

1. Today's Highlights

The LiquidAI LFM3 family lands in force: core support for LFM3-1.7B / LFM3-VL-2B (b11938), video input plumbing for the same family (#31283), a /v1/realtime voice-chat path (#31269), and decision-model variants d1-2B / d1-omni-2B (#31275). 2. Releases & Breaking Changes

Rapid release cadence continues (b11927 through b11938 in ~24h). Notable items:

  • b11929 — common: --model or -hf is now required. CLI invocations that previously fell through to an implicit default will now error out. Scripts and CI wrappers should pass an explicit model path or Hugging Face repo. https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases
  • b11930 — new --models-memory-max server flag (router mode): enables dynamic unloading of models when the combined resident footprint (including a to-be-loaded model) exceeds a byte threshold. This is opt-in; existing behavior is unchanged if unset. https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/21231
  • Windows CUDA prebuilt binaries appear frozen at b11828 while tags advance past b11852 — an ongoing packaging discrepancy, not an upstream code issue. Track #31085. https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/31085
  • No API breaking changes to libllama or the HTTP server surface in this window (the reasoning-effort capability probe in #31271 is additive).

3. New Model & Hardware Support

Item Type Link
LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B + LFM3-VL-2B core support New models b11938 / #31252
LFM3 video input (incl. video + soundtrack) mtmd / convert #31283

Note: d1-2B/d1-omni-2B (#31275) is closed — verify whether it merged or was superseded by the LFM3 work before relying on it.

4. Performance & Optimization

  • Server memory management (b11930, #21231): --models-memory-max computes load-time memory requirements (via no_alloc) and evicts resident models when the next model would exceed the budget. Directly targets multi-model router deployments where the working set exceeds VRAM/RAM.
  • Sparse attention / KV selection (b11936, #31243): k-pool sparse selection (Qwen4-EXP/QSA, GLM5-next) is now built independently of kq_mask shape — a necessary decoupling for index-based cache-cell selection at long context.
  • Metal TOP_K mask fused kernel (b11927): single-pass -inf fill + kept-cell copy per row, replacing separate scorers. Reduces sampler overhead, especially relevant for speculative decoding draft batches.
  • Hexagon TOP_K (PR #31279): reported as 42% of DFlash draft batch time and 25% of DSpark on X2 Elite with full-vocab (248k) TOP_K per draft row. New kernel avoids full per-tile sort.
  • ggml-vulkan MUL_MAT dim-3 broadcast (b11933, #31239): unblocks mul_mm/mul_mmq/mul_mat_vec paths previously rejected by supports_op, fixing llvmpipe CI and enabling broader shader coverage.
  • MoE expert cache spill to CPU (PR #30966): --moe-cache-cpu-share executes cache-missed experts on CPU; decode speed impact depends on host memory bandwidth.
  • Test infra (b11934, #31145): model saving no longer instantiates a llama_context, and tensor generation drops std::normal_distribution for a faster sampler — shortens the test feedback loop.
  • OpenCL tiled q4_K lm_head GEMM (PR #30412): batch > 1 path for vocab-scale q4_K weights on X2-90 / Adreno 830/840; previously GEMV-only layout.

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity and reproducibility:

  1. Quantized-target speculative decoding divergence (#25618, 32 comments, OPEN). Under greedy sampling (temp=0, top_k=1), draft-model spec decode produces different text than non-speculative runs when the target is Q4_K_M-class; bf16 targets match. This is a correctness bug, not a perf issue — output is silently wrong. No fix PR referenced yet. https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/25618
  2. CUDA graphs hang GPU channel on RTX 5090 Laptop / sm_120 (#27330, OPEN). RC watchdog + Xid 8; GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 is a complete workaround. https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/27330
  3. -np 2 --kv-unified prompt processing drop of 42–54% from the second long request onward (#28495). Root cause identified: CUDA/HIP FA kernels skip only KQ-mask tails, not interior all--INF blocks, so sequences pay for foreign KV cells. Known limitation, no fix landed. https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/28495
  4. Vulkan device-lost class of bugs — multiple open: Vega 8 iGPU at ~50K ctx (#26447), R9700 server crash with ctx-checkpoints (#27560), RX 6900 XT (#27076), Radeon 680M with --load-mode auto (#27360, mmap avoids it), Intel Gen9.5 UHD 630 q8_0 KV hang (#29054, vk::Error escapes as std::terminate). Vulkan remains the least stable backend for long-context and large-model workloads.
  5. SYCL issues: DFlash2 draft triggers Windows TDR reset on dual Arc B70 (#28778); bad output on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (#28728); OOB/VRAM overcommit kernel panic addressed by temporary guard PR #31285.
  6. CUDA IQ3_S produces garbage on RTX 5060 Ti / Blackwell (#28581) — quantization × architecture interaction worth verifying before serving IQ3_S on sm_120.
  7. Security-adjacent: ggml_nbytes() integer overflow permitting OOB read via malicious tensor in the RPC path — fix PR open (#31217). Relevant if you run ggml-rpc-server against untrusted peers.
  8. Vulkan count_experts.comp inefficiency (#31163): zero_skipped_rows() loops over all expert IDs per thread — performance defect, not correctness.
  9. Fixed/closed: ROCm split-mode garbage output (#16424), tensor-split memory leak on dual Intel B70 SYCL (#27845), Ling 3.0 autoparser tool-call terminator (#27462), ngram-cache per-slot cache leak across requests (#27852 — acceptance 86%→11%, worth reading if you enable ngram spec decode).

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Router-mode multi-model serving is now first-class. If you multiplex several models behind one llama-server, adopt --models-memory-max (b11930) rather than hand-rolling eviction. Pair with --models-memory-max accounting that includes the incoming model's size — it does this for you.
  • Pass --model/-hf explicitly after b11929. Audit launch scripts and Docker entrypoints.
  • Do not ship speculative decoding on quantized targets without an eval gate. #25618 means your Q4_K_M + draft-model pipeline can silently emit different text than your non-spec baseline under greedy decoding. Either validate against a bf16 target in CI or run speculation off for correctness-critical paths.
  • LiquidAI LFM3 is now a viable local stack for multimodal + voice. LFM3-VL (vision), LFM3-Audio/Omni (voice chat via /v1/realtime), and the d1 decision models cover perception-plus-routing in a 1.7–2B envelope. Attractive for on-device agents where a frontier VLM is overkill.
  • MiniCPM-OCR-Jev (#30980) is a scorer, not a generator — it produces a scalar judgment, so wire it as a validation/ranking node in an agent graph rather than a text endpoint.
  • Blackwell/IQ3_S and Vulkan long-context remain risk areas. For production on sm_120 use Q4_K_M/Q5_K_M and validate; for Vulkan prefer --load-mode mmap and keep ctx below the reported failure thresholds (heading toward 50K+ on iGPUs).
  • RPC exposure: if you run ggml-rpc-server in a shared or untrusted network, track #31217 — the overflow is a memory-safety issue in the tensor-size check path.
  • Metal users get cheaper sampling via the fused TOP_K mask (b11927) — measurable on Apple Silicon spec-decode and any wide-vocab sampler config.

Ollama Digest — 2026-10-28

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases shipped in the last 24 hours, but the issue tracker is unusually active on agent-loop and tool-calling correctness: a Qwen3.8 /api/chat streaming failure (#17778, 32 👍), a DeepSeek-V4-Flash thinking-loop on Cloud (#17892), and silent dropping of out-of-schema function calls (#19187) all point to agent reliability as the current pain point. On the infrastructure side, two large MLX PRs land in-progress support for Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B with speculative decoding (#19229) and concurrent MLX generation via OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL (#19197), plus a first fix for LFM3 GGUF loading (#19344).

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

No new releases in the last 24h.

Two behavior changes worth tracking for anyone pinning versions:

  • #19292 — /v1/systemone rejects decision-head GGUF models since 0.40.4. Models declaring CAPABILITY decision without a decision.type key now return HTTP 400 (worked on 0.40.3). Affects custom decision/classifier heads.
  • #19155 — Cloud /v1/responses returns 413 for ~10.7 MiB requests well under the model context window. A related in-flight PR (#19309) adds a single compaction retry with a smaller serialized summary after a bare 413.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • #19229 — mlx: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B (open). Adds per-layer expert configs, LiLiCorr speculative decoding through the existing DFlash runner, prequantized affine 3-bit import with per-module metadata, and mixed-precision expert stacking.
  • #18780 — mlx: Kolibri 1 support (open), authored by jmorganca.
  • #19344 — LFM3 GGUF fixes + llama-server TTS. Honors explicit tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token=false (fixes LFM3 and lfm2:24b template BOS stripping); text-to-speech path activates once llama.cpp advances past b11901. This is the fix for the "unknown model architecture: 'lfm3'" failure in #19347 and the MLX-runtime complaint in #19343.
  • #19329 — AMD Radeon RX 6750 GRE 10GB (Navi 23) support request. Open, no PR.
  • #19338 — discover: use newest library version supporting all GPUs. Fixes stale anyMissing state in filterOverlapByLibrary that caused the newest CUDA/library bundle to be permanently rejected after any partial GPU match failure. Relevant to mixed-GPU hosts.

4. Performance & Optimization

  • #19197 — mlx: concurrent generation via OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL (open). Ready requests share projection and feed-forward work; attention remains per-request. Default stays at 1 — higher parallelism consumes proportional memory. Directly relevant to the OOM complaints in #19262, where OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1 did not visibly serialize two Goa sessions.
  • #18978 — retry llama-server startup with eager CUDA module loading (open). Fixes CUDA error: shared object initialization failed in fattn_mma on partial-offload loads (RTX 5060 Ti + 16 GB host RAM). Addresses #19122 and the Vulkan-adjacent slowness report in #13567.
  • #19326 — scheduler evicts by model path on keep_alive ties (open, no PR). findRunnerToUnload sorts by sessionDuration then model path; with uniform keep_alive the deciding key is lexicographic path, not recency or size. Predictable but surprising behavior for multi-model deployments.

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. Qwen3.8 /api/chat 500s in tool loops — #17778, open, 32 👍, 56 comments, updated today. ResponseError during chat streaming: no user query found in messages at 205k context while the model iterates tool calls. Highest-signal bug in the tracker.
  2. DeepSeek-V4-Flash:0731 thinking loop on Cloud — #17892, open. Same reasoning paragraph emitted 221 times over ~1m45s, zero usable output, only 4 tool calls. No `` marker involved — not a template-marker issue.
  3. Silent drop of out-of-schema function calls — #19187, open. qwen3:8b calling a tool not in the request's tools yields an empty response with eval_count > 0. Fails closed without an error — dangerous for agent orchestration.
  4. macOS Metal crashes in MLX runner — #19278 (kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorImpactingInteractivity) and #18885 (panic: mlx on M6/16 GB). Both open.
  5. Windows connection resets after ~15s on large prompts — #19139, open, needs more info. Ollama 0.40.4, RTX 3090, 24 GB.
  6. Broken q2_K/q3_K quantizations of qwen2.5-coder:3b-instruct — #18252, open. 0/15 on a functional smoke suite where sibling quants score 87–100%. Official library artifacts; worth pinning.
  7. Pull resume broken after >1h server restart — #19337. Fix PR #19339 keeps interrupted downloads resumable across restarts.
  8. DNS64 / NAT64 pull failures — #19345, open. hf.co CDN resolves to 64:ff9b::/96, rejected as non-public. Blocks all ollama pull hf.co/... on DNS64 networks.
  9. REPL state bugs — #19340 (Ctrl+C mid-multiline leaves REPL stuck in multiline mode) and #19341 (/load resets messages but not opts.System). Both open, both from the same reporter, both low-blast-radius.
  10. OpenAI-compat: empty-content assistant messages lose tool_calls — #19151, closed. Relevant if you replay history with "content": [].

Also closed today: #19303 (ollama launch opencode fails on OpenCode v2 due to array-typed debug config), #19155 (Cloud 413).

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Treat tool-call loops as a first-class failure mode. #17778, #17892, and #19187 are three distinct manifestations of the same class of problem: the model, the parser, and the server disagree about turn boundaries. If you're building agents, add your own wall-clock and iteration caps rather than relying on the model to terminate, and log eval_count alongside empty responses — #19187 fails silently.
  • Pin your quants. #18252 shows official library artifacts can be functionally dead at specific quantization levels with no error at load time. Validate against a functional eval set, not just perplexity.
  • Concurrency semantics are still settling. MLX models on OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL > 1 land in #19197; OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1 on the llama-server path is disputed in #19262. If you size memory budgets around serialized inference, verify empirically on your version.
  • Cloud has its own limits. #19155 (413 on ~10.7 MiB) and #19309's compaction retry mean large coding sessions need client-side request compaction; don't assume the advertised context window is the operative limit.
  • EE / network-constrained environments should test ollama pull hf.co/... explicitly before relying on it — #19345 breaks the entire path on DNS64 resolvers with no workaround short of changing resolvers.
  • Windows + partial offload + Blackwell is the least-covered configuration in today's data (#19139, #19122). If that's your deployment target, budget for the CUDA eager-load retry in #18978 and watch for the fix to land.

Today's Highlights

A heavy release cadence continues across four stable lines (v1.106.5, v1.105.6, v1.104.8, v1.103.10), but the most consequential work today is in the PR queue: a large guardrail-security cluster (MCP hidden-tool bypass, secret redaction in tool traffic), a gzip-scoping backport being cherry-picked onto both 1.105.x and 1.106.x, and a batch of [risk:high]/breaking changes around key expiration and user-directory scoping. On the ops side, a still-unbackported eMudhra root CA fix on stable/1.106.x remains the sharpest open supply-chain concern for anyone shipping 1.106.x images.

Releases & Breaking Changes

  • Backport: gzip scoping (#48680, #48679) — on both 1.105.x and 1.106.x, every response over 500 bytes is currently gzipped (including inference streams/tokens) and sub-1 MiB bodies are compressed on the event loop, stalling other requests. Cherry-pick of #46712 lands in v1.106.6 / v1.105.7. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/48680 · https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/48679

  • xAI X Search (#48677) — native support via the Search API and WebSearch interception; returns citation URLs as results and records xAI-reported billing (tokens + tool usage). https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/48677

  • Streaming fast path restored (#47735) — a request-only guardrail was forcing the per-chunk response check on every streamed token; the gateway now skips it unless a guardrail actually inspects streamed pieces. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/47735
  • Router Redis round-trip reduction (#48645) — shared session-tier pin read now joins pending Redis work, saving one round trip; fixes cross-worker tier-pin coherence for identical tool continuations. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/48645
  • CI guard speedup (#48683) — spend-logs-guard and cost-map-guard drop the Rust extension build + 157-package install, cutting 3–5 min runs to seconds. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/48683

Ranked by severity:

  1. MCP hidden-tool bypass (HIGH) — a tool excluded from tools/list by a pre_mcp_call guardrail remained callable by exact name. Two fixes merged: #48187 (enforce on tools/call/mcp_tool_call) and #48669 (refuse before upstream execution, incl. calls without prior listing). https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/48171 · https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/48669
  2. Secret leakage in tool traffic (HIGH, PR open) — [risk:high] #47122 extends hide-secrets to tool results, tool inputs, tool call arguments, and system prompts for coding agents; every other guardrail sees unchanged input. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/47122

  5. Silent upstream + request_timeout never fires (#38358) — streaming request to an upstream that accepts TCP but never writes a byte hangs past litellm_settings.request_timeout. Closed. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/38358
  6. MCP parallel-request slot leak (#46093) — every streamed /v1/messages carrying a web_search tool permanently consumes one max_parallel_requests slot. Closed. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/46093
  7. Budget reservation sized by max_input_tokens (#47396) — Anthropic-format tool_choice on /v1/messages triggers a token_counter KeyError and over-reserves budget. Closed. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/47396
  8. /v1/messages message_start reports zero usage (#48481) — Chat Completions adapter emits input_tokens: 0 on the first stream event; real counts land in message_delta. Closed. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/48481
  9. reasoning_effort: "none" removes thinking config instead of disabling it (#47924) — on default-on Claude models the upstream default silently re-enables thinking. Open. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/47924
  10. 500 instead of 400 on non-object JSON bodies (#43711) — []/scalars hit AttributeError in pre_db_read_auth_checks. Closed. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/43711
  11. SpendLogs partition misalignment (#34364) — partition boundaries shift when DB session timezone ≠ UTC. Open. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/34364
  12. Guardrail header lists unexecuted steps (#48472) — x-litellm-applied-guardrails and spend logs over-report after early pipeline stop. PR open. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/48472

What This Means for Application Developers

  • If you pin 1.105.x or 1.106.x, plan the gzip upgrade now. Until v1.106.6/v1.105.7, inference responses are compressed on the event loop, and any client that mishandles Content-Encoding on streaming bodies can corrupt tokens. Pin to the patched build once published.
  • Agent builders should treat MCP tool discovery as authoritative. The listing-then-calling bypass is now blocked both at call time and before upstream execution — but if you cached tool names client-side to bypass tools/list, re-verify the allowlist semantics. Likewise, the hide-secrets expansion to tool args/results/system prompts (#47122) will change what agents see in tool history.
  • Budget enforcement is not yet trustworthy at the edge. The #27735 stale-spend discrepancy plus #47396's max-input over-reservation mean you should keep your own hard caps on key spend and not rely solely on BudgetExceededError as a customer-facing boundary.
  • Timeouts on streaming paths need a belt-and-braces approach. #38358 shows /v1/messages and completions can hang past litellm_settings.request_timeout when an upstream is silent from the first byte; add an application-level watchdog for agent loops.
  • Cosign verification remains a first-class part of the release process — every tagged release ships a cosign.pub and reproducible verification commands; wire this into your image-promotion pipeline before deploying to production.
Unsloth — unslothai/unsloth

Unsloth Digest — 2026-10-28

Today's Highlights

No releases shipped in the last 24h, but the repo is in a heavy stabilization push: a batch of CI/test fixes from the core team (torch dynamo/inductor config drift, pytest pinning, import-hoist verifier), plus several correctness/perf fixes for Studio (safetensors context overflow, MLX 4-bit decode speed, Stop responsiveness, ChatML role casing). On the feature side, the Flows editor rebuild (Studio component/theme parity) and the Benchmarks expansion (llama-bench, lm-eval-harness Evals tab) are the most substantive in-flight PRs. Hardware coverage debates continue: AMD iGPU VRAM accounting, Intel Arc finetuning, and exllamav3 are all open requests.

Releases & Breaking Changes

None in the last 24h.

Note for API consumers: PR #15417 reports that the Anthropic passthrough endpoint /v1/messages returns a hard 400 exceed_context_size_error on context overflow instead of applying auto-compaction — a behavioral inconsistency vs. the OpenAI-compatible path. Not yet fixed.

New Model & Hardware Support

  • LFM3-1.7B support requested (LiquidAI LFM3 family, new backbone) — issue #15588
  • Intel Arc B580 (XPU) finetuning workflow question/open request — issue #15583
  • exllamav3 (exl3 quants) inference engine support requested; prior PR stalled — issue #15527
  • AMD multi-GPU: PR #14039 excludes iGPU shared-RAM from Train-page VRAM totals and default GPU pick (fixes bogus 100 GiB reporting on dual R9700 + Ryzen iGPU systems)
  • MLX / Apple: Gemma 4 26B MLX vision producing <unused6226> tokens — issue #15473; mixed NVIDIA+AMD Linux detection broken under custom llama.cpp — issue #15444

Performance & Optimization

  • MLX 4-bit chat (~30% decode speedup): Studio now keeps embeddings and output head in 4-bit for MLX-loaded safetensors (e.g. Qwen3-0.6B ~350 → ~460 tok/s) — PR #15617
  • GGUF tokenizer load (50–200 ms CPU saved per read): string arrays (150k–262k tokens/merges) now walked through a single buffer instead of per-entry read/unpack/seek; cold loads read the header multiple times — PR #15593
  • Linux sandboxed tool spawn: removal of Python pre-exec (_sandbox_preexec) reduces per-call launch overhead — PR #15625
  • Desktop launch: login-shell PATH probe no longer blocks window open (previously unbounded wait) — PR #15567
  • Benchmarks expansion: llama-bench tab for real prompt-processing/generation throughput, plus lm-eval-harness Evals tab (MMLU, MMLU-Pro, HellaSwag, ARC-C, GSM8K, TruthfulQA) — PR #12522, PR #12521
  • Image/video API queueing: POST /v1/videos now queues during an active render (was 409), and waiting /v1/images/generations batch — PR #15613

Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. CI-wide breakage (torch config drift) — torch._dynamo.config.recompile_limit, suppress_errors, _inductor.config.emulate_precision_casts no longer exist; 55–70 errors per PR across Backend CI shards. Fix PRs open: PR #15626, PR #15624
  2. Context overflow on safetensors → opaque "internal error" across Studio chat, OpenAI-compat, and Anthropic-compat APIs; crash is a tensor size mismatch. Fix: PR #15616
  3. Anthropic passthrough /v1/messages fails on overflow instead of auto-compacting — breaks coding agents that rely on compaction; no fix PR yet — issue #15417
  4. Online DPO + use_vllm=True crashes at trainer init (UnboundLocalError: generation_kwargs) for LoRA, full FT, and fast_inference — fix: PR #15598
  5. Windows training floods Recycle Bin with sqlite WAL/SHM temp files (~10k entries / ~40 MB in 90 min) — issue #15552
  6. Memory leak: ~200–400 MB loss on C: per use, no cleanup path — issue #14487
  7. Stop button unresponsive on MLX while prompt is still being read (non-batched replies: Tools on, JSON format, logprobs) — fix: PR #15615
  8. ChatML datasets with capitalized roles silently produce empty rows on Qwen3/Phi-4, halting training — fix: PR #15599
  9. Studio training stack trace — issue #15538
  10. Qwen3.5-2B Studio resume fails: _MODEL_WEIGHT_RE misses model.safetensors-00001-of-00001.safetensors — issue #15405

What This Means for Application Developers

  • Pin your torch: if you build on Unsloth CI or vendor its test harness, expect dynamo/inductor config symbol removals to break test suites until #15626/#15624 land. Pin pytest < 9.2 in the interim.
  • Handle overflow explicitly in client code: the Anthropic passthrough path does not auto-compact — implement your own truncation/summarization before hitting /v1/messages, or route through the OpenAI-compat endpoint where compaction works.
  • Safetensors serving is safer for chat after #15616, but until merged, wrap generation calls with explicit context-length pre-checks and don't rely on generic error messages for diagnostics.
  • Mac/MLX users get a material throughput win from #15617; if you're benchmarking inference cost on Apple silicon, re-measure after that lands. Also track #15615 if you enable Tools, JSON mode, or logprobs — Stop semantics were broken there.
  • GPU inventory logic matters on mixed systems: the AMD iGPU fix (#14039) shows VRAM totals can be inflated by shared system RAM — validate device selection in your own orchestration layer rather than trusting the UI's default GPU pick.
  • Agent builders: multi-agent orchestration (#10776), full-page screenshots for Browser Use (#15448), optional visual Computer Use (#15532), and MCP per-tool switches (#14348) are all queued — if you're integrating agents via MCP or browser tools, watch #14348 for the config surface you'll need to support.

Official AI Content Report 2026-10-28

Today's update | New content: 6 articles | Generated: 2026-10-28 00:25 UTC

Sources:

  • Anthropic: anthropic.com — 5 new articles (sitemap total: 491)
  • OpenAI: openai.com — 1 new articles (sitemap total: 1090)

AI Official Content Tracking Report

Date: 2026-10-28 | Sources: anthropic.com / claude.com, openai.com | Incremental Update

1. Today's Highlights

Anthropic dominated today's release cycle with five substantial pieces spanning IPO registration, a major government partnership, and three research publications — an unusually dense cadence that signals a company in a coordinated "scale-up and capital-markets" phase. The most consequential items are the S-1 filing with the SEC (proposed Nasdaq listing under the ticker "ANT") and the expanded GSA partnership offering a 40% government-wide discount projected to save the public sector ~$1 billion. On the research side, Anthropic published defensive/offensive security work (five real-world exploit chains found by an unreleased internal model), a human-factors study on how AI agents shape expert judgment, and progress reports from its life-sciences drug-development program. OpenAI's only incremental item is a metadata-only listing for "Oracle Apps in ChatGPT," which — while not summarizable from available text — suggests further enterprise application integration activity, though this cannot be confirmed from the crawl.

2. Anthropic / Claude Content Highlights

📢 News / Corporate

Anthropic files S-1 with the SEC for proposed initial public offering

  • Category: news | Published: 2026-10-26 (crawled 2026-10-27)
  • Link: https://www.anthropic.com/news/s1-sec
  • Core insight: Anthropic, PBC filed a Form S-1 for a proposed IPO of Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "ANT." Share count and price range are undetermined; Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are named underwriters.
  • Strategic significance: The filing formally converts Anthropic from a private, mission-structured PBC into a public-market story. For enterprise and government buyers, this introduces a new dimension of scrutiny (disclosure, quarterly cadence, shareholder pressure) alongside its safety positioning. It also reframes the competitive narrative: Anthropic is signaling durability and scale to procurement officers who historically favor incumbents with public financials.

Expanding our partnership with GSA to bring Claude to all levels of government

  • Category: news | Published: 2026-10-27
  • Link: https://www.anthropic.com/news/expanding-partnership-gsa
  • Core insight: A new GSA agreement gives government buyers a 40% discount across Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government, and the Claude API — applying to direct purchases today and cloud-provider purchases "in the coming months." The discount extends to state, local, tribal and territorial governments, and is coupled with a dedicated implementation program.
  • Adoption metrics cited: ~500 US federal/state/local organizations now use Claude; weekly Claude for Government active users up ~8x since February; federal civilian agency usage up ~20x in a year. Estimated government savings: ~$1 billion.
  • Strategic significance: This is a land-and-expand play for the public sector — locking in procurement channels at every level (federal → SLTT) and pre-empting competitors in a market characterized by long procurement cycles and tight budgets. Bundling API access into the discount is notable: it pressures agencies to build on Claude rather than treat it as a single-seat tool.

🔬 Research

Discovering and exploiting vulnerabilities in critical, real-world software with Claude

  • Category: research | Published: 2026-10-27 | Team: Frontier Red Team
  • Link: https://www.anthropic.com/research/discovering-vulnerabilities-with-claude
  • Core insight: Using an unreleased, internal research model, Anthropic produced five full attack chains against widely used software — including one-click remote code execution in Chrome, a one-click exploit chain in Safari, an Android lock-screen bypass, a Windows remote denial-of-service, and zero-click RCE in Linux.
  • Process detail: Vulnerabilities were reported under Anthropic's coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy (90 days to patch, plus 45 days before detailing beyond public advisories).
  • Strategic significance: This is a dual-purpose signal. It (a) demonstrates frontier cyber-offense capability to justify its own safety framing, and (b) asserts a defensive posture — positioning AI-assisted vulnerability research as a net security benefit while implicitly arguing for controlled release of such capabilities. The explicit mention of an "unreleased" model is a deliberate capability teaser for the safety and policy audience.

How AI agents shape experts' judgment calls

  • Category: research | Published: 2026-10-27 | Team: Alignment (Amaç Herdağdelen, Hailey Joren, Alex Tamkin)
  • Link: https://www.anthropic.com/research/agents-judgment-calls
  • Core insight: 50 professional analysts with causal-inference experience used Claude Code to advise a farming cooperative. The study varied whether the agent surfaced decision points to the human, testing whether experts truly retain judgment or defer to the agent.
  • Strategic significance: This is among the earliest rigorous, task-realistic studies of agent-induced judgment erosion — a governance-relevant risk for enterprise deployment (accountability, auditability, decision provenance). The study design (four discrete choices between two reasonable options) is a template others may replicate. For enterprise buyers, it surfaces a compliance argument: agent output must be transparently bifurcated from human judgment.

Early progress on accelerating drug development with Claude

  • Category: research | Published: 2026-10-27 | Team: Science
  • Link: https://www.anthropic.com/research/early-progress-drug-development
  • Core insight: Anthropic's life-sciences team is in deep research partnerships with six organizations — BigHat Biosciences, Bristol Myers Squibb, Divergence Labs, Enveda, Generate Biomedicines, and The Column Group — and has begun drug discovery efforts of its own.
  • Framing: The team argues bottlenecks are distributed across the entire pipeline (target ID → molecule design → manufacturability → regulatory filings → trial design), not just in molecular generation. Anthropic plans to "scale this work up substantially."
  • Strategic significance: This moves Anthropic from model provider to domain participant in biopharma — a vertical with extreme regulatory scrutiny and high-value data. "Our own drug discovery efforts" is the key phrase: it implies vertical integration and potential IP generation, not just tooling.

📊 Research Cadence Note

Four of five Anthropic items published/dated Oct 26–27 cluster tightly (S-1, GSA, and three research pieces), indicating a coordinated release window. Three distinct research teams (Frontier Red Team, Alignment, Science) all published on the same day — an unusually high cross-team cadence that may reflect a pre-IPO effort to demonstrate breadth across safety, security, and applied science.

3. OpenAI Content Highlights

⚠️ Data Limitation Notice

OpenAI's incremental update for 2026-10-28 contains one item with no article text. The title is derived from the URL slug and may be inaccurate. Per methodology, no content summary or interpretation is fabricated below.

Oracle Apps in ChatGPT

  • Category: index | Published: 2026-10-28
  • Link: https://openai.com/index/oracle-apps-in-chatgpt/
  • Status: Metadata-only. No article body available in this crawl. The slug suggests an Oracle enterprise-applications integration surface within ChatGPT, but this cannot be confirmed from available data. No research/release/company/safety categorization is possible without source text.

Analytical note: No inference about feature scope, availability, or enterprise terms should be drawn from this entry alone. A follow-up full crawl is required to characterize this item.

4. Strategic Signal Analysis

Anthropic's Recent Priorities

Priority Evidence
Capital markets / scale S-1 filing; Nasdaq ticker "ANT"; tier-1 underwriters
Public-sector ecosystem GSA 40% discount across all product surfaces; SLTT expansion; dedicated implementation program
Frontier safety & security research Five real-world exploit chains via an unreleased internal model; CVDisclosure rigor
Alignment / human-AI interaction Expert judgment study; agent delegation risk
Vertical applied science Six biopharma partnerships + own drug-discovery efforts

The through-line: Anthropic is simultaneously broadening commercial reach (government, life sciences) and deepening its safety/research credibility — a deliberate pairing ahead of a public listing, where both revenue durability and responsible-AI positioning must be defensible to institutional investors and regulators.

OpenAI's Current Signal (within data limits)

Only one incremental item, metadata-only, at an enterprise-application integration slug. No cadence or thematic claim can be responsibly made from a single, text-less entry. Comparing "who leads" vs. "who follows" is not supportable from today's OpenAI data alone — any such comparison would be speculation.

Competitive Dynamics (qualified)

  • Anthropic is setting today's agenda by volume and strategic breadth (IPO + government + three research verticals).
  • OpenAI's single metadata entry suggests activity in enterprise-app integrations, which — if confirmed by a future crawl — would position it in adjacent enterprise-software territory. This is a hypothesis to verify, not a finding.
  • A genuine competitive read on public-sector vs. enterprise integrations requires at least one more OpenAI data point with body text.

Impact on Developers & Enterprise Users

  • Developers: The GSA agreement's inclusion of the Claude API under a government discount is a concrete procurement lever; agencies can standardize on Claude at the API layer, not just the UI.
  • Enterprise / regulated buyers: The expert-judgment study is directly compliance-relevant — it provides citable evidence for designing agent workflows with human decision provenance.
  • Security teams: Anthropic's disclosure of real exploit chains (with a 90+45-day responsible-disclosure protocol) sets an expectation that frontier labs will both find and coordinate disclosure of critical vulnerabilities — a new baseline for vendor risk assessment.
  • OpenAI-dependent teams: Hold judgment on "Oracle Apps in ChatGPT" until source text is available; today's crawl supports no integration details.

5. Notable Details

  1. Ticker "ANT" + PBC status. Anthropic retains "PBC" (public benefit corporation) in its S-1 language while listing Class A shares — a first-order governance signal worth tracking in the final prospectus.
  2. API explicitly discount-eligible for government. Prior government discounts often targeted seat-based enterprise tiers; extending to the API under GSA is a notable escalation toward platform-level standardization.
  3. Cloud-provider purchases within scope ("in the coming months"). This pre-announces a channel expansion — agencies buying via hyperscaler marketplaces will inherit the same 40% discount. Vendors and resellers should model pricing impact.
  4. "Unreleased, internal research model" in the vulnerability post. A deliberate capability teaser: it demonstrates a tier above public models specifically in cyber-offense, feeding both capability marketing and safety-policy arguments.
  5. "We've also begun drug discovery efforts of our own." First explicit statement that Anthropic is doing internal discovery — a signal of vertical integration and potential IP, distinct from partnership-only positioning.
  6. Expert-judgment study uses Claude Code. Frames the agentic coding surface (not chat) as the locus of judgment-delegation risk — consistent with enterprise deployment trends.
  7. Cross-team research density on one day (Oct 27): Frontier Red Team + Alignment + Science. Three distinct teams publishing simultaneously is unusual and may signal either a coordinated pre-IPO showcase or a quarterly research push.
  8. Government adoption metrics as a public benchmark: "~8x since February," "~20x in a year," "~500 organizations," "$1B savings." Anthropic is publishing quantified public-sector traction — a metric set that will likely recur in investor materials.
  9. OpenAI data gap itself is a signal of crawl limitation, not necessarily of OpenAI inactivity — the 2026-10-28 crawl returned only a title-derived entry. Do not interpret the absence of body text as absence of substance.
  10. "Oracle Apps in ChatGPT" is the first Oracle-specific integration slug surfaced in this tracking window. Pending confirmation, it would represent continued enterprise-app expansion; treat as unverified.

Report compiled 2026-10-28. OpenAI section constrained by metadata-only input; all OpenAI claims limited to URL and category per methodology.
